title: NPCBench: A Clinical Apprenticeship Benchmark for Guideline-Constrained Care-Pathway Reasoning in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
claim: A benchmark mirrors specialist training by linking component skills to patient-level longitudinal pathways, scored with joint-correctness metrics beyond isolated tasks.
layout: 3 panels: top clinical scenario, bottom-left skill levels, bottom-right longitudinal evaluation
description: A dense three-panel figure with pastel purple and teal backgrounds. Panel (a), at the top, shows the NPC clinical scenario. On the left is baseline evidence: endoscopy and pathology slides, an MRI scanner with scans, and icon tiles for symptoms, labs, EBV DNA and exams. On the right is a care-pathway flow (Workup, Diagnosis & Stage, Treatment, Management, Follow-up, Progression) with an NCCN/CSCO guideline box. Panel (b), at the bottom left, stacks levels L1–L6 and O1. Each is a small mini-pipeline, covering guideline memory, atomic application, multimodal grounding, case planning, longitudinal revision, CarePath (100 patients, 417 tasks) and consult rubrics. Panel (c), at the bottom right, shows an evidence stream feeding a timeline of visits, with state-change branches in dashed red and green. Below the timeline are three metric cards: Decision Acc., All-care and Joint Success. A banner states that high step accuracy does not equal a successful pathway.
caption: Overview of NPCBench. (a) NPC care combines pathology, MRI, biomarkers, and clinical records under guideline constraints. (b) The apprenticeship framework spans component skills, longitudinal revision, and CarePath evaluation; O1 assesses consultations. (c) Changing patient states drive reporting of local and joint correctness. CarePath evaluates each decision using the provided clinical context; separate serial controls examine feedback from prior answers.
abstract: Current medical benchmarks typically break down clinical competence into isolated factual questions, single-image tasks, or static case vignettes. These tests score individual answers, but reveal less about whether a model can integrate subspecialty knowledge with multimodal evidence and track a patient's condition throughout a course of care. To close this gap, we introduce NPCBench, a clinical apprenticeship benchmark for nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). NPCBench mirrors specialist training, from guideline and foundational knowledge to case planning, longitudinal review, CarePath integration, and open-ended consultation. It contains 4,777 component and consultation items and a 100-patient CarePath cohort with 417 scored diagnostic and care tasks. The episode-level evaluation tests whether diagnostic and care answers are jointly correct within a care pathway. By linking stepwise tasks to patient-level care trajectories, NPCBench evaluates whether models ground decisions in visual evidence, interpret changes in patient state, and meet clinical requirements in consultation. Across 30 evaluated models, we observe a composition gap: strong performance on individual tasks does not ensure jointly correct diagnostic and care answers for the same patient. Among 21 multimodal models, strict CarePath success reaches at most 23%. Paired controls and physician calibration further examine evidence grounding, longitudinal revision, and consultation judging. Overall, NPCBench broadens the evaluation of medical artificial intelligence beyond static question-answering paradigms to an apprenticeship-oriented assessment of clinical workflows, thereby offering a testbed for evidence-based and temporally coherent reasoning in oncology care.
